content:
alex: seeing sustained 95th+ latency spikes when preemptible jobs are overflowed into reserved eu-west pools this morning. heatmap attached?

maria: confirmed. started ~06:20 UTC. spike coincides with the daily batch job ramp.

sven: are we spilling to the right pool? sounds like capacity mismatch (short seq jobs hitting long seq instances)

alex: yes — current routing rule uses spare GPU count only. no SLO awareness. probably routing short-running low-latency tenants to P100 nodes.

devin: monitor-bot: alert: pool-eu-west-reserved-3 latency_p95 > 1200ms for 10m

claire: hmm. we should prefer routing by latency SLO + seq_len distribution. can we add a quick heuristic: if tenant p95 > 300ms, avoid sending their overflow to pools with >40% long-seq jobs?

maria: +1. also preemptible spillover shouldn't prefer machines with colder NVMe caches (warm kv cache matters).

sven: proposed short-term fix: shard overflow by "latency class" computed from last 5m qps + tail latency. fallback: route to dedicated low-latency reserve lane.

alex: prototype rule (on staging):
```
route_if(spare_gpus>0) {
  if(tenant.latency_class=="low") prefer(pool.tag=="low-latency")
  else prefer(pool.tag=="throughput")
}
```

devin: can we implement latency_class cheaply? maybe approximate via avg_seq_len and recent p95 from tracer?

maria: yes. tracer has p95 per-tenant windowed metric. we can compute latency_class in router service and attach as header to placement requests.

claire: also need cost guardrails. routing more low-latency tenants to reserved low-latency pools increases unit cost. must add a budget token bucket per customer so we don't explode spend.

alex: action items:
- implement router-side latency_class lookup (devin)
- add a per-tenant budget token bucket for low-latency pool ejections (maria)
- run a 1h canary in eu-west (sven)

sven: I'll schedule the canary at 09:00 UTC and monitor p95 and NVMe hitrate.

monitor-bot: deploy-bot: canary started: eu-west/latency-aware-routing v0.1 at 09:00 UTC

devin: quick note — watch out for oscillation: moving tenants between pools can change seq_len distribution. add hysteresis (10m) to routing decisions.

claire: agreed. add 10m cooldown + require 2 consecutive windows.

alex: thanks everyone. if the canary stabilizes, plan to roll to eu-central next to check az boundaries.

maria: FYI +postmortem if it hits >3% error increase. tagging @oncall

devin: copying config snippet to ops playbook in case of rollback.

alex: closing for now, will post follow-ups after the canary.
